passage: Creche note, Thursday. Farhan has just turned one and joined our room this month. This week I noticed him light up with a wide smile, mouth open, when I bent over his mat, and again when the cook, Mala, called his name from the door. Each time I smiled back and said, “Hello, Farhan,” and he answered with a gurgle, then looked at me again as if waiting. I will keep greeting him face to face at his level. 🙂 Ganga

qa.q: Who wrote the note, and when?
qa.a: Ganga, signing at the end, wrote the creche note on Thursday.

qa.q: What might Farhan's wide smile and waiting look mean?
qa.a: Probably pleasure and a wish to keep the exchange going, since he smiled, gurgled and looked back at her. He might also just be reacting to a friendly tone of voice.

qa.q: What is Ganga's plan and why might it work?
qa.a: She will greet him face to face at his level. Smiling back gives him a response, which helps him learn that his signals get answered.

qa.q: How might Mala's greeting feel to Farhan?
qa.a: Hearing his name from a familiar voice can feel welcoming, so he smiles at her too, showing he already links her with warmth.

grounding: A young child gives broad social smiles to familiar faces, and the adult's returned smile builds the exchange.

passage: On the verandah in the afternoon light, Swati sat with her baby Yogesh in her lap, wiping his face after his rice. He looked up at her and his mouth opened into a huge, gummy smile, arms waving. Swati smiled back and tilted her head. “Oh, is that for me?” Yogesh cooed and smiled again, watching her eyes. Her mother-in-law, passing with a basket, grinned at the pair. Swati waited a beat, then said his name softly and got another smile in return, like a small back-and-forth.

qa.q: What was Swati doing when Yogesh smiled at her?
qa.a: She was wiping his face after his rice while he sat in her lap on the verandah.

qa.q: What does Yogesh seem to feel when he smiles at Swati?
qa.a: He seems pleased and connected to her, since he waves his arms and keeps watching her eyes. It could also be a response to her friendly voice, not yet a message meant for her.

qa.q: Why does Swati's smiling back matter?
qa.a: It shows him that his signal gets an answer, and it starts a conversation of attention. She can keep taking small turns with him.

qa.q: How might Swati's mother-in-law see the moment?
qa.a: She may see a mother and baby learning each other, and it may bring back memories of her own children's first smiles.

grounding: A young child gives a broad open-mouth smile to a familiar face, and the mother's smile back builds the early back-and-forth.
